TABLE 4.1: Chart of LMV phonetic and phonological features. ... feature source(s) Atakapa Biloxi Chit. MTL Natchez Ofo Tunica Western Muskogean ... 24 tone Kaufman 2012 0 0 0 0 1 0 0 0 ... Ejective stops, /kw/, /ŋ/, /r/ (including /r/ and /l/ opposition), /tl/, preaspirated voiceless stops, vowel harmony, and pitch/tone are present in two or fewer languages of the region, and, in accordance with my definition of a Sprachbund, are not relevant in determining the LMV as a Sprachbund.
tone_statements.summary: Areal survey: tone scored absent (0) for Chitimacha, tonal contrast said to occur only in Natchez among LMV languages; no basis given for the Chitimacha coding; Chitimacha sketch lists segments only.

sources.quote: Sec. 57.2.1: 'Chitimacha also has the rare (Gordon [2016]) characteristic that statements have a final rising intonation, and questions have a final falling intonation ... Within a word, the first syllable is always stressed (Swadesh [1946]a: [313]).' BUT footnote 1: 'Because Chitimacha places stress on the final syllable of each word, most American linguists pronounce the English name with final stress ... the modern Chitimacha term for the language is Sitimaxa /si.ti.ma.xa/, with stress on the final syllable.' tone.summary: Nothing on tone or pitch; the one prosodic remark makes accent a non-distinctive matter of phrase rhythm, falling on the phrase-final syllable. Chitimacha forms are cited without accent marks.
